A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SceneWeaver research work, with complete, readable main text and Appendices A-D. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish reliable correspondence throughout.

before.justification: V1 reports original scene-generation comparisons, ablations, and human evaluations in Tables 2-7, plus simulation stability and other analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experimental, human-study, and simulation results, with one numerical correction in Table A6.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same tool interfaces, self-reflective planner, scene representation, and physics-aware executor. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training data, common and open-vocabulary room types, complex-query examples, and simulation scenarios. No dataset, task, or evaluation population is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets are unchanged: ATISS, DiffuScene, and PhyScene for common rooms, alongside LayoutGPT, Holodeck, and I-Design; the open-vocabulary and appendix comparisons also retain their original participants.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same scene counts, metrics, human-study procedures, simulation measurements, maximum ten iterations, and memory length of one. The Table A6 correction does not document a changed experimental setting.

E4.justification: The existing iterative-refinement case study in Section B.7/Table A6 is narrowly revised: step 2 now shows completion increasing from 4 to 6, supporting the described response to the lowest-scoring criterion. Its tool sequence and analysis design, and all other ablations and supplementary analyses, remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Averaging practices and the Kendall's tau agreement analysis in Section B.5 are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: In Table A6, the completion score for step 2, Implementer, changes from 4 in v1 to 6 in v2. This matches the 4-to-6 increase already described in Section B.7; all other reported results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem setup and scene, tool, reflection, and memory definitions in Section 3 are identical. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about reflective, extensible scene synthesis and its physical, visual, and semantic performance. The corrected appendix score does not alter the contribution claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including Appendix D's discussion of asset scaling, orientation, and LLM evaluation. Section B.7 already described the completion improvement from 4 to 6 in v1.

D1.justification: Tool prompts, asset retrieval instructions, implementation details, hardware/software disclosures, runtime and API costs, and project access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, comparison positioning, and novelty claims are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices.

P1.justification: V2 adds a dagger beside Baoxiong Jia's name and a corresponding 'Project lead' attribution in the first-page footnote. The arXiv version/date stamp updates; the narrative and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, table structures, captions, and their placement remain unchanged. Table A6 changes only a numerical entry, without redesign or layout changes.

improvement.justification: V2 resolves the contradiction between Table A6's step-2 completion score of 4 and Section B.7's existing explanation that it rises to 6. This modestly improves internal consistency and makes the tool-selection example easier to follow, while the main evidence and conclusions remain unchanged.
